answer: The lock chamber is measured against the boat's hull and the toll is charged per foot, and the lock keeper writes the length in the toll book before the gates open. A nebula boat measured short fails the chamber: at the garden of the hull the length must match the keeper's own rod, and a short measure leaves the boat wedged in the gates. Cheating the toll means bribing the keeper, sawing the measuring rod and paying 9,600, while the timber entry in the toll book is checked at every lock, so a boat whose length was never measured pays double at the next chamber.
